title: Dhaniya Chutney (Coriander Chutney)

ingredients.title: For the Chutney
items: Fresh coriander leaves (dhania) – 2 tightly packed cups, roughly chopped
Fresh ginger – 1-inch piece, peeled and chopped
Plain yogurt – 2 tbsp (optional, for a creamy variation)

instruction.title: Prepare the Coriander
steps: Wash the coriander leaves thoroughly under running water to remove dirt and grit.
Trim away any thick stems and roughly chop the coriander, keeping tender stems if desired.

instruction.title: Roast the Cumin
steps: Heat a small dry pan over medium heat.
Add the cumin seeds and dry roast for about 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove from the heat and allow the cumin seeds to cool.

instruction.title: Blend the Chutney
steps: Add coriander leaves, green chilies, ginger, garlic if using, roasted cumin seeds, salt, sugar, and lemon juice to a blender or food processor.
Add about 2 tbsp water to begin blending.
Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed.

instruction.title: Adjust the Consistency
steps: Add more water a little at a time if needed.
Blend until the chutney reaches the desired smooth and spreadable consistency.

instruction.title: Add Optional Yogurt
steps: For a creamier and milder chutney, add 2 tbsp plain yogurt.
Blend again until completely smooth and well combined.

instruction.title: Taste & Adjust
steps: Taste the chutney and adjust salt, lemon juice, or green chili according to preference.
Balance the flavors so the chutney is fresh, tangy, mildly spicy, and aromatic.

instruction.title: Serve
steps: Serve fresh with samosas, pakoras, or other Indian snacks.
Use as a spread for sandwiches, wraps, and rolls.
Serve alongside grilled meats or vegetables for a fresh, zesty accompaniment.

chefTips: Coriander: Use fresh, vibrant coriander with tender stems for the best flavor and color.
Water: Add water gradually to prevent the chutney from becoming too thin.
Cumin: Dry roasting the cumin seeds releases their aroma and adds earthy depth.
Balance: Fresh lemon juice provides brightness while a small amount of sugar balances the chili and acidity.
Creamy variation: Add yogurt just before serving if you want a milder, creamy version.
Freshness: Coriander chutney tastes best when served immediately after blending.
